description: Housed in the historic Royal Overseas League headquarters where Scottish explorers once stayed, 100 Princes Street evokes a stylish private club for urban adventurers. Custom furnishings and handpicked antiques adorn the 30 unique, tartan-lined rooms and suites; many boast direct views of Edinburgh Castle. Enjoy local comfort fare (Aberdeen Angus burgers, lentil cottage pies) and rare Scottish whiskies in the plush dining room, The Wallace. Hotel staff provide “anything, anytime” service, while a bounty of attractions lie at your doorstep.
inTheKnow: Tailored experiences range from fly-fishing on the River Tweed to creating your own Scottish gin to curated tours for Harry Potter superfans.
summary: Setting a new standard in luxury hospitality, 100 Princes Street is poised to become a beloved destination for those seeking an exclusive, immersive and opulent Scottish experience. Located in the heart of Edinburgh, within the storied walls of what once was the headquarters of the Royal Overseas League, 100 Princes Street is an exquisitely curated haven that promises an adventure into Scotland’s rich cultural and historic legacy. Echoing the ambiance of an elite members' club, 100 Princes Street offers an exclusive escape into a world where tradition and modern luxury converge.

description: Surrounded by 185 wooded acres and steeped in French history, Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay is the chosen country escape for Paris’s well-heeled set. This medieval Cistercian abbey and former Rothschild estate now welcomes guests with 145 unique, antique-filled rooms and six distinctive dining experiences. Take a boat out on the lake, cycle around the parkland, join a masterclass, and watch movies in the private cinema. An impressive wellness spa, housed in the old stud farm, offers sound baths and aerial yoga.
inTheKnow: Every Saturday and Sunday, guests can enjoy a lavishing brunch in Le Réfectoire des Moines, which exudes an enchanting Hogwarts-inspired ambiance where constellations of candles illuminate arches.
summary: Like an immense playground in the heart of unspoilt nature, the Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay promises to make every moment a waking dream. With its attentive service to the highest degree, the enveloping intimacy of its rooms, the generosity of its communal spaces as grandiose as they are warm, and the infinite range of its activities, the estate transports us into this incredible family home 45 minutes from Paris. Over the course of the 4 seasons, by the fire or by the lake, between rejuvenation, earthly nourishment and exceptional moments, everyone writes their own Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay experience.

description: The landmark Abi d’Oru perches above a private stretch of sugar-white beach along the Gulf of Marinella. Each of the airy rooms and suites features a balcony or terrace, most with sea views; choose between contemporary and traditional décor. Lounge by the pool or indulge in a spa treatment using Sardinian honey and essential oils while the kids play in the supervised water park. Dining options include fresh seafood and Italian fare; sample the suckling pig, an island specialty.
inTheKnow: Memorable experiences range from yacht cruising and jet-skiing to rock-climbing and exploring prehistoric nuraghi. For authentic island flavor, enjoy a mountainside lunch with Orgosolo shepherds.
summary: Marinella beach, one of the most beautiful in Sardinia, lies just beyond the garden, the pool and the natural pond. Fine white sand meets a turquoise sea that shimmers through every imaginable shade of blue as it fades into the horizon. A section of the beach is reserved for guests of the Abi d’Oru and equipped with loungers and umbrellas, this is also the most sheltered area on breezy days. The new for 2026 Summer "Trattoria del Pescatore" Restaurant evokes the timeless essence of summer holidays. It offers guests everything they need to savour to the full the delights of a long day spent on the beach.

description: The 186-room Alila Shanghai transforms the city’s vibrant Jing’an district into a tranquil urban sanctuary. Its serene design—utilizing natural stone, warm timber, rattan details, and lush greenery—creates a nature-infused retreat. Enjoy cocktails on the Secret Roof terrace before dining on traditional Shanghai cuisine or grilled Japanese robatayaki. Holistic spa treatments merge modern therapies with traditional Eastern practices. This resort-style hotel sits adjacent to the historic Zhangyuan shikumen complex, and guests enjoy special access to these beautifully restored stone-gate townhouses.
inTheKnow: Slip into stillness with a complimentary gong sound bath, create your own incense or learn the ancient art of knot button-making. It’s an easy walk to Jing’an Temple and shops along West Nanjing Road.
summary: Alila Shanghai places you in the historic Jing’an district, surrounded by Shanghai’s rich history and culture and yet just a short distance from this coastal city’s modern existence as a center for business and finance. Nearby, discover ancient traditions of artisans, Shanghai Grand Theatre, museums, shopping and more. When your journeys are complete, return to your urban oasis built with comfort, luxury and sustainability in mind. Restore your body and spirit with a visit to the tranquil Spa Alila, a quiet moment in our library, a meal or tea at our restaurants, or some time at our Secret Roof bar featuring craft cocktails and outstanding views.

description: Just a mile from famed Buddhist temples lies a secret forest garden and Aman Kyoto. Surrounded by ancient woodlands that once offered refuge to a revered artist community, this secluded sanctuary pays homage to the traditional ryokan (Japanese inn), albeit in strikingly modern style. Moss-covered stone pathways wind between latticed pavilions that house 26 minimalistic rooms; healing onsen baths source their waters from nearby mineral springs. Practice yoga, take a mindfulness hike, or explore Kyoto’s 17 UNESCO World Heritage sites.
inTheKnow: Take your cultural experiences to the next level during a traditional tea with a geiko, meditation at Daiouin Temple, or practicing the art of Ikebana flower arranging.
summary: A remarkable setting, at one with the city's artistic soul Aman Kyoto represents the fruition of a beautiful landscape first conceived as the garden of a textile museum. Whimsical stone pathways curve gently along the forest floor, and stone slabs blanketed in moss serve as the foundations for the resort's architecture. The secluded grounds are part of what was an artistic community that gave rise to the revered Rinpa school of painting some 400 years ago, and are within easy reach of Kyoto’s most important sites, including the stunning golden temple, Kinkakuji.

description: Neo-Renaissance grandeur meets refined modern aesthetics at Aman Venice. description: Amangalla, set on the ramparts of Galle Fort, welcomes those who relish the chance to relive history. An easy walk through the historic fort has you taking in the old Dutch church, spice warehouses, the lighthouse, and Court Square. Return to your home base, for its palm-tree-lined swimming pool and its rejuvenating spa – therapies are customized for each guest, incorporating hydrotherapy pools, saunas, steam rooms, and plunge pools. Your bedroom is adorned with an antique four-poster bed, pettagama chest, wooden floors, freestanding bathtub, shower room, and views of the fort or the mature gardens.
inTheKnow: There’s a small alcove on the second floor where you can enjoy a drink as the sun sets over Galle Fort’s colonial rooftops. Open the windows and let Sri Lanka in! - Carrie Wallace Chicago, Illinois
summary: The stately grande dame of Galle Fort, a World Heritage Site on Sri Lanka’s south coast, Amangalla boasts all the period charm of a bygone era. Combining the Sanskrit-derived word for ‘peace’ with galla, Sinhalese for the town of Galle, the hotel stands at the junction of Church and Middle Streets with commanding views of the Fort’s ramparts. With its chandeliers and soaring fin de siècle ceilings, being welcomed into Amangalla’s Zaal, or Great Hall, is like stepping into the past. It houses the elegant Dining Room at one end and a cocktail station at the other, with a welcoming lounge area in between – ideal for enjoying a cup of Ceylon tea or an evening cocktail accompanied by live music.…

description: Amangiri (which means “peaceful mountain”) is set in Utah’s stunning canyon country and incorporates the beauty of the Four Corners desert into its design. The central pavilion, built around a dramatic swimming pool, houses the living room, gallery, library, and dining room/cellar. Amangiri’s 34 suites and 1 private four-bedroom home offer modern, airy living, dining, and sleeping areas with white-stone floors that echo the area’s natural stone; some provide private plunge pools and rooftop terraces. Be sure to experience the Aman Spa, with its water pavilion, Pilates studio, candlelit rooms, and outdoor treatment terraces.
inTheKnow: A must-do activity: climbing the Studhorse Via Ferrata (Iron Road). No previous experience is necessary, and the views are out of this world! –Chad Clark Phoenix, Arizona
summary: An otherworldly desert retreat, Amangiri is situated on 900 pristine acres in Canyon Point, Utah with sweeping views towards Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument. Located in the centre of the Grand Circle, the all-season resort, its landmark Aman Spa and its secluded camp known as Camp Sarika by Amangiri are surrounded by such iconic attractions as the Grand Canyon, Monument Valley, and Bryce and Zion National Parks. The region has been home for centuries to the native Navajo tribe and presents the raw landscape for which the American Southwest is famed. description: Everything about Amanjena is mesmerizing, including its 32 sunset-hued guest pavilions, each with a wood-burning, sunken fire pit for romantic interludes and a terrace with a cozy, cushioned seating area. The seven two-story maisons are like elegant Moroccan townhouses, each with inward-facing windows, a wall fountain, and a marble-columned bathroom – there’s even a private swimming pool and garden. Slip away to the full-service spa, with its truly Moroccan hammam and essential-oil massages; you’ll be invited to soak in a rose-petal bath and sip mint tea. Be sure to explore the numerous souks, with their countless treasures.
inTheKnow: For a memorable evening, have a romantic, private dinner in your courtyard surrounded by hundreds of candles. –Jean Pickard Atlanta, Georgia

Lying within an oasis of palm and olive trees close to the ancient city of Marrakech and its famous Unesco-protected Medina, the resort lies adjacent to the 27-hole Amelkis Championship Golf Course. Known in Arabic as Al Medina al-Hamra, the ‘Red City’, due to its rose-hued structures, Marrakech was the inspiration behind Amanjena’s design. The resort’s walls echo the city’s old pisé (rammed-earth) buildings as well as the Berber villages that cling to the High Atlas Mountains. Green is also a predominant colour – the colour of paradise, royalty and abundance. Amanjena’s 18 rose-toned…

description: Amanjiwo is right at home in central Java, rich in culture, spirit, and beauty. At the center of the resort is a soaring, bell-shaped rotunda, from which the guests can see the UNESCO-protected Borobudur temple. Dining facilities includes the dining room and terrace, lively bar, and Roman-influenced swimming pool. After settling into your lavish suite, with its volcanic-ash-tinted roof, handcarved furniture, and exotic Javanese fabrics, take time to explore the myriad cultural and archaeological opportunities that abound in this region. The resort can arrange excursions by car, electric bicycle, or horseback.
inTheKnow: Join the Mystical Element of Borobudur tour and watch the sun rise over temples while listening to stories from the exceptional guides. –Tisha Neufville Roswell, Georgia
summary: Amanjiwo (“peaceful soul”) is fashioned out of limestone and takes its inspiration from the surrounding culture of Central Java. The resort is located within a natural amphitheatre with the limestone Menoreh Hills rising directly behind, the Kedu Plain in front and four volcanoes – Sumbing, Sundoro, Merbabu and Merapi – gracing the horizon. Amanjiwo looks out onto Borobudur, the largest Buddhist sanctuary in the world. Amanjiwo’s suites feature terrazzo flooring, high ceilings, domed roofs and sliding glass doors that open onto a garden terrace with a view of Borobudur or surrounding farmland. Fifteen suites come with private swimming pools. All suites include a thatched-roof balé…

description: Set on a verdant hillside next to a cliff and overlooking East Bali’s Lombok Strait, Amankila is welcoming in every respect. From your freestanding suite, connected to the resort’s public areas and restaurants by stepped walkways, to the Beach Club, where water sports are available, you’ll feel at home – yet so very far removed from your workaday life. Water lovers adore the two resort outriggers, designed to emulate traditional Balinese fishing craft – cruises are offered daily. Visit two of the island’s most important temples, Lempuyang and Besakih, the former of which is considered one of Bali’s “six temples of the heavens.”
inTheKnow: Arrange for a morning snorkeling cruise aboard one of the resort’s private boats – breakfast is served on board, and there’s a plush top deck for sunbathing.
summary: Amankila (which means "peaceful hill") set on a cliffside overlooking the Lombok Strait in East Bali, offering beach and mountain resort experience in one location. Amankila’s suites are elevated to take advantage of the spectacular views to the sea and surrounding hillsides. The 31 free-standing suites, with their alang alang roof thatching, are fashioned as beach houses with a twist. All suites are connected to the reception and restaurant area by stepped walkways. description: Imagine a kingdom where “gross national happiness” is paramount, where culture and tradition hold strong, and where Buddhism has predominated since the 7th century. Amankora operates five unique lodges in complete harmony with their environment, offering an inside look at the rich culture and beauty of this stunning region. Stay at Amankora Thimphu, in a blue-pine forest; in Amankora Gangtey, overlooking a 16th-century monastery; or in Amankora Bumthang, neighbor to Wangdichholing, the palace of the first and second kings. Paro and Punakha lodges offer countless opportunities to explore the valley, visiting monasteries and temples.
inTheKnow: Be sure to book a stay at the Punakha lodge. In spring it offers a warm, subtropical contrast to your Bhutan adventure – plus it comes with an amazing infinity-edge pool. –Ally Daisa, California
summary: Amankora Paro, Amankora Punakha, Amankora Gangtey, Amankora Thimphu and Amankora Bumthang offer a unique experience of Bhutan’s impressive dzongs (fortress-monasteries), historic lhakhangs (temples) and pristine Himalayan landscapes, opening access to traditions unchanged over centuries. Sited in the picturesque Paro Valley near Balakha Village, 20 minutes from Paro’s only international airport, Amankora Paro is a 24-suite pine forest retreat commanding dramatic views of the 17th century Drukyel Dzong and the snow-clad peak of Mount Jhomolhari at an elevation of 7,300 metres. description: Overlooking the spectacular Vinh Hy Bay in Vietnam, Amanoi is a tranquil retreat. Named after the Sanskrit-derived words for “peace” and “place,” this luxury resort features 31 pavilions and villas, two wellness pool villas and 11 residences, all offering privacy, serenity, and beauty. In the serene Aman Spa, guests can indulge in massages and treatments created with traditional Vietnamese ingredients, such as aromatic herbs, rice, and coffee. And in the resort’s beach club, located on a beautiful, private, white-sand beach, you can lounge, dine, swim, and enjoy a complete range of water sports, from snorkeling to kayaking.
inTheKnow: Soak in the culture and try a few popular local dishes. Don’t miss out on bánh căn (Vietnamese rice pancake) during afternoon tea at the Main restaurant and catch-of-the-day seafood in the Beach Club.

Named for the Sanskrit-derived word for ‘peace’ and noi meaning ‘place’, Amanoi is a tranquil retreat situated on a beautiful white-sand beach overlooking spectacular Vinh Hy Bay. Shaped like an elegant seahorse with its back to Laos, its tail embracing Cambodia and its belly curving into the western waters of the East Sea, Vietnam is one of Southeast Asia’s most fascinating countries. Its scenic coastline stretches in a sinuous s-shape over 3,200 kilometres from China in the north, to the Mekong Delta and beyond in the south. description: Blending seamlessly into its mystical environment, Amansara is set in the former guesthouse of King Sihanouk – it was originally a guesthouse for dignitaries visiting the region’s ancient ruins and temples. Today’s guests visit those same spectacular sites, including spiritual Angkor Wat, through off-the-beaten-path excursions via custom-made remork (moped-powered trishaw). Here, 24 Indo-Chinese-style suites offer private courtyards, and half of them boast private swimming pools. The Spa is a haven of tranquility with its therapeutic Cambodian rituals, offered in four dark-wood treatment rooms.
inTheKnow: Try the hotel’s exclusive Angkor Wat tour, with access to a secret back entrance. You’ll beat the crowds and be in the ultimate position to watch the stunning sunrise. –Lily Read London, England
summary: Minutes from the sacred temples of Angkor – a Unesco World Heritage Site – Amansara is a peaceful sanctuary on the outskirts of Siem Reap. A masterpiece of 1960s New Khmer architecture commissioned by King Norodom Sihanouk for his guests, today the residence houses 24 sleek Suites, along with a soaring circular dining room and a holistic spa. The original pool has been replicated amid tranquil mature grounds, and many of the Suites feature private gardens and plunge pools, adding to the introspective atmosphere. description: Amanyangyun is more than a resort – it is a living piece of China’s heritage. Set on the outskirts of Shanghai amid a relocated forest of thousand-year-old camphor trees, the property comprises more than a dozen Ming and Qing dynasty village buildings, reassembled stone by stone and complemented by minimalistic, contemporary spaces, all connected by paved pathways and ornamental ponds. The result is a tranquil, 24-suite retreat where time slows, allowing guests to contemplate the graceful choreography of a traditional tea ceremony or therapeutic benefits of the spa’s dual bathing rituals.
inTheKnow: The hotel’s largest reconstructed building has been transformed into a cultural center where guests can learn and practice traditional arts, such as calligraphy, or watch a kunqu opera performance.
summary: Just outside downtown Shanghai, a cherished camphor forest sets the scene for Aman's fourth destination in China: Amanyangyun. Meaning ‘nourishing cloud’, yangyun is a reference to expanding the ‘cloud’ of the mind with knowledge – a philosophy borne by the story of the trees and dwellings at Amanyangyun's heart. This introspective retreat belies a remarkable tale of a forest transported, and a history preserved.

description: Escape completely at Ilha de Bazaruto, set within a protected marine park some 24 miles off Mozambique’s mainland. Guests can arrive via a complimentary 45-minute boat transfer, or opt for a charter flight (there’s even a private landing strip). Just 44 luxury villas dot these still untouched shores, where rolling sand dunes melt into azure waters favored by migrating humpback whales. Indulge in locallyinspired spa treatments, dive along protected reefs, swim with dolphins, try dune-boarding, or take a sunset cruise.
inTheKnow: Ocean views are on the menu at Tartaruga, where dinners of local fare like flame-grilled meats and local seafood are served on the idyllic beach.
summary: With 2,500 km of Indian Ocean coastline, Mozambique is an aqua-playground bathed in brilliant watercolour hues. Nowhere is its beauty more pristine than the Bazaruto Archipelago, a protected marine reserve and national park. Ilha de Bazaruto, Island of the Mist, lies 30 km off the mainland. Here, rolling sand dunes melt into clear azure ocean. Swim with dolphins and experience the annual migration of humpback whales from July to September. Set sail for the sunset. Lose yourself to nature’s beauty in one of the last untouched paradises. Welcome to Anantara Bazaruto Island Resort, a truly luxury escape among Mozambique resorts.

description: Across 99 guest rooms and nine suites, Appellation Healdsburg is a rising star in Sonoma County, within a few minutes' drive of northern California's finest wineries. The woodsy wine-country design by architect John Hill merges nature with modern comfort: think luxe fire pits surrounded by Adirondack chairs and sliding barn doors leading out to olive trees and on-site gardens. It all unfolds over two distinct "villages," spread over nearly nine acres. Guests and locals gather at Andys Beeline Rooftop for sweeping vistas, winding conversations, and craft cocktails.
inTheKnow: Community is big here: savor a human-and-canine "Yappy Hour" on the first Thursday of every month; an evening with a winemaker every Friday; and yoga classes on Saturdays, free for resort guests.
summary: Healdsburg is more than a stay—it’s an immersion into the flavors, textures, and spirit of Sonoma County. Designed by acclaimed architect John Hill, the resort’s two distinct villages are intentionally placed to invite exploration, with winding paths leading past mature native trees, abundant culinary gardens, and open-air gathering spaces. Whether unwinding by one of two swimming pools, indulging in restorative treatments at the spa, or savoring seasonal flavors at our Charlie Palmer-led restaurants and bars, every moment is crafted with a sense of place.

Today, new archaeological discoveries suggest the ancient civilized cities date back to 12000 BC. summary: Belvedere Hotel Mykonos Nestled in the heart of Mykonos Town, the Belvedere Hotel is an island icon with a legacy dating back to the 1920s, when the property began as the Campanis family's private villa. Open spaces, thoughtful design, and proximity to the island's finest galleries, restaurants, and boutiques create a truly unmatched experience. description: The Negev Desert covers nearly half of Israel, but perhaps no stretch is as dazzling as the dozen acres that encircle Beresheet. Built on the rim of Makhtesh Ramon – the world’s largest crater – the hotel masterfully blends into the silent landscape, with a scattering of one- and two-story buildings housing 111 contemporary rooms (be sure to book one with a balcony or with your own pool overlooking the crater). The gourmet restaurant, which serves locally sourced, organic cuisine, appears to be suspended above Makhtesh Ramon. Explore the crater on a safari or cycling tour, or simply appreciate its grandeur from the infinity pool.
inTheKnow: Take some time to explore Mitzpe Ramon’s Spice Route Quarter, where former military hangars have been transformed into cafés, boutiques, and artist studios.

description: One of the Garden Route's most celebrated and best-loved hideaways, Birkenhead House is as dramatic as it is cozy and private. The white-pillared hotel is set atop a craggy cliff; between July and December, you might glimpse a passing whale (for an even closer view, take the tour departing from Kleinbaai Harbour). From here, it's easy to visit the Hemel-en-Aarde Valley, known for its amazing vineyards and jaw-dropping scenery. The area is home to some of South Africa's finest examples of pinot noir and chardonnay. Rooms are as decadent as they come; ask for the one with a romantic clawfoot tub set in the middle of the bathroom.
inTheKnow: At the right time of day when the tide is just right, you’ll be able to walk down to the beach in front of Birkenhead House with one of our chefs and pick fresh mussels from the rocks.

description: Heed the call of the wild at Blanket Bay, one of New Zealand's premier lodges. Take a horseback ride along the shores of Lake Wakatipu or visit local wineries. Cozy up in your sumptuous room, with its private terrace overlooking the natural splendor. Dinner, served in the lake-view Evening Dining Room or on the outdoor terrace, is complemented by your choice of the region's finest pinot noirs, rieslings, and chardonnays.

description: On a private street between Via Montenapoleone, Via della Spiga, La Scala, and the Accademia di Brera, in a tastefully renovated 18th-century Milanese palazzo, is the Bvlgari Hotel Milano. Golf carts help you navigate the vast grounds, which include tennis courts, a private beach, and a dazzling infinity pool that merges with the sea. Go sailing, cycle along the coast, or explore nearby Palma de Mallorca.

summary: Cap Rocat is much more than a hotel: it is an architectural and environmental conservation project, as well as a tribute to all travellers who understand that visiting a new place contributes towards creating a legacy of love and respect for other cultures and ways of life. description: Legendary, historic, associated with romance, celebrities and glamour, the Carlton Cannes has traversed the ages and earned its status as a unique and authentic haven that values its memory and its soul.

summary: At the 58 boulevard de la Croisette, the Carlton Cannes is preparing for its rebirth. In all its glory, the jewel of the French Riviera opens a new chapter in its history. The hotel has not experienced such a transformation since its opening in 1913. Now, 110 years after opening, the “Grande Dame” enters a new century and maintains its entire renovation and extension project, with a reopening scheduled in 2023. Nothing is more beautiful than those moments of imagination before the journey, the instant when it bodes tomorrow’s horizon. Life at the Carlton Cannes begins anew yet is as sublime as ever.

description: It’s easy to see why Ravello, and the entire Amalfi Coast, has inspired the likes of Richard Wagner, D.H. Lawrence, and Gore Vidal. The Caruso has long been a favorite of discerning globetrotters. Just 50 guest rooms and suites make for an intimate ambience, and most of the rooms have a sea view, terrace, or private garden. Outside, the infinity-edge swimming pool sits dramatically suspended between sea and sky. Join the head gardener for a private tour of the terraced gardens and enjoy the complimentary boat cruise along the Amalfi Coast, then reserve a romantic candlelit dinner at the open-air Ristorante Belvedere.

Its origins date from the 11th century when the noble d’Afflitto family, having been shipwrecked off the coast, fell deeply in love with the romantic setting. description: Giuseppe Cipriani (the inventor of Bellini) brings his namesake luxury hotel to Italy with the opening of Casa Cipriani Milano. Unwind in the well-appointed spa featuring Finnish saunas, a green onyx-covered steam bath, and a Hammam. description: The history of Normandy lives on in its chalk cliffs, D-Day beaches, and the timeless walls of Château d’Audrieu. This 18th-century manor, set amid 62 acres of parkland, traces its roots back to the 11th century. Its noble heritage endures through gilded moldings, crystal chandeliers, and heirloom antiques, blending elegance with authenticity. A meticulous renovation has elevated its charm with a Sothys spa, 29 luminous guest rooms, and a Luxury Tree House hidden among the branches. At Le Séran, Chef Samuel Gaspar showcases the flavors of Normandy through seasonal menus inspired by the château’s gardens and local producers.
inTheKnow: Spend slow, sun-dappled days cycling along Normandy’s coastline or wandering the gardens,a serene retreat and a perfect starting point to explore Mont-Saint-Michel and the timeless French countryside.
summary: About Us Between Caen and Bayeux, the Château d’Audrieu opens its doors to a journey through time. This 18th-century monument, listed as a French historical landmark, combines the grandeur of heritage with the warmth of a family home. Surrounded by 25 hectares of parkland designed by Louis Benech, the Château unfolds its elegance through tree-lined pathways, centuries-old oaks, and gardens that bloom with every season. Here, history whispers in every stone and the air carries the gentle rhythm of Normandy. description: A jewel of 18th-century Quattrocento architecture nestled in the heart of Provence, Château de Fonscolombe is both a family estate and a sanctuary of serenity. Its 50 acres of vineyards, historic lounges, heated pool, and 50 rooms and suites offer a moment of complete repose. Guests can wander through parks dotted with centuries-old trees, indulge in curated wellness experiences, or savor the seasonal, environmentally conscious cuisine of Chef Marc Fontanne at La Table de l'Orangerie and Le Temps Suspendu. Every experience is designed to celebrate the Provençal art of living, blending elegance, comfort, and a sense of discovery.
inTheKnow: Take time to disconnect and embrace the Provençal rhythm, morning walks in the gardens, afternoons by the pool, and long gastronomic lunches followed by sunset apéritifs surrounded by vineyards.
summary: Nestled just minutes from Aix-en-Provence, Château de Fonscolombe invites guests into three centuries of French art de vivre. This 18th-century Provençal estate, once home to the Marquis de Saporta, has been meticulously restored by Hélène Martel-Massignac and her team, honoring both its heritage and its timeless elegance. Designed as a grand family home, the Château balances shared spaces with intimate privacy. Fifty rooms and suites open onto luminous salons where echoes of sumptuous receptions still linger, adorned with Genoa leathers, 18th-century Chinese wallpapers, and ceilings adorned with Provençal gypseries. description: The Château La Chenevière’s understated humility belies its 18th-century grandeur. This 29-room country house hotel, located near the Normandy landing beaches, was occupied by both Axis and Allied forces during WWII. Today, it provides a peaceful retreat where you can stroll through aromatic rose gardens or bike around the 30 acres of ancient cedars and sequoias; interiors exude a warm Gallic charm with floral wallpaper and antiques. The refined Le Botaniste serves regional dishes complemented by an impressive cellar, and the two-hectare permaculture garden provides vegetables and herbs for both this restaurant and Le Petit Jardin.
inTheKnow: The pyramid-shaped orangery is particularly stunning at night, as you watch lights reflect off the heated pool while savoring lunch or dinner from Le Petit Jardin.
summary: A former mansion and farm, this magnificent Norman chateau of the eighteenth century, “La Chenevière”, finds its charm in the testimony of the times it went through. Constructed in an area dedicated to the cultivation of hemp in the eighteenth century, then a breeding farm for exceptional foals during the nineteenth century, the chateau was occupied by the Germans during World War II, and then the Americans after the D-Day landings. It was fully restored in 1988 to become the lush hotel-restaurant that it is today. La Chenevière has now 29 spacious and comfortable rooms that reflect the elegance and romance of its design. description: Step into the Sun King's world at Château Louise de La Vallière, a sixteenth-century jewel rising from the forests of Touraine. Twenty signature rooms and suites—each with dedicated butler service—transport you to the era of Louis XIV; staff in period costume enhance the immersive experience. Unwind at the spa, swim in the heated outdoor pool, and stroll the 47-acre park. description: COMO Maalifushi was created for those who seek a remote, luxury escape. Find Asian therapies at the award-winning COMO Shambhala Retreat, with overwater spa pavilions. Water activities – diving, fly-fishing, and surfing – offer multiple opportunities to explore the region. The resort’s signature COMO Shambhala Kitchen is also available – rich in living enzymes, vitamins, and minerals.

Guests can also enjoy yoga and holistic Asian therapies at the COMO Shambhala Retreat, with the entire guest experience defined by COMO’s exacting, passionate service.

description: Situated in the heart of Hamburg, Conrad Hamburg is nestled within the Leventehaus, which is a protected architectural landmark built in 1912 by Franz Bach. Sip top-shelf spirits at the intimate cigar lounge before taking a gastronomic journey across Latin America in the signature restaurant, Greta Oto. The 1,000 m² (10,764 sq ft) spa and fitness area features a 20-meter pool, sauna, steam bath, along with a comprehensive selection of treatments.

description: Located just outside Telluride, Dunton Hot Springs breathes new life into a 19th-century ghost town. description: A storied hideaway perched on the iconic rock in sunny St Barths. In 1950, Rémy de Haenen purchases the rocky promontory and builds a hotel upon it, gambling on the island’s potential as a dream destination. description: Sleek, dramatic, and drop-dead gorgeous, the 56-room Emiliano encapsulates the modern Brazilian ethos. Land your chopper on the private heli-pad, then be escorted by service-oriented butlers, and head to the country’s first Champagne and caviar bar, where more than 80 brands of bubbly and rare Beluga roe await you. Soak in the Japanese hot baths before a shiatsu massage at the spa, and then take a table at the hotel’s namesake Italian restaurant for house-made pasta and organic, local produce. The fashion houses and galleries along Rua Oscar Freire – São Paulo’s version of Rodeo Drive – lie just beyond the lobby’s window wall.

summary: Emiliano Sao Paulo is Brazil’s finest example of world class luxury hospitality. Located on Oscar Freire Street, in the heart of the exclusive Jardins neighborhood of Sao Paulo, the Emiliano Hotel sets the pace for a new age of luxury travel in Brazil. Our guests experience authentic and modern Brazilian sophistication through our contemporary ambience, refined cuisine and singularly warm service. Detail orientation is what best defines the Emiliano Hotel. From the clean lines and spaciousness of our award-winning architecture to our finely selected amenities, everything at the Emiliano has been carefully designed to maximize the comfort of our guests.

description: Experience the pampas without the pomp at Estancia la Bamba de Areco, Member of Relais & Châteaux. A long avenue lined with plane trees leads to the colonial-style building, which features 11 rooms adorned with dark woods and local artwork and textiles. Go bicycling, get a hot stone massage, or join a maté tea tasting; you can watch the gauchos display their equestrian skills or join a trail ride. After a dinner of steak and other traditional fare, relax with a glass of wine while the cowboys entertain with folkloric songs and dancing. The estancia hosts an international polo team, which regularly plays on the property’s two fields.

description: The famously otherworldly Atacama Desert is known for its volcanoes, sand dunes and lunar-like valleys that roll up to the edge of dark skies filled with dazzling stars. Straddling it all, Explora’s lodge at Atacama offers something rare: elevated, award-winning accommodations just two blocks from the historic town of San Pedro de Atacama and yet contained entirely within this luminous desert. All-inclusive and open year-round, its 50 hacienda-style rooms (46 rooms and four suites) and sweeping modernmeets-adobe architecture span a 42-acre estate with native gardens, quiet paths, a spa and multiple pools framed by tall grasses.

description: In December 2018, conservationists Kristine and Douglas Tompkins pioneered the creation of the 750,000-acre Patagonia National Park. Today, this biodiverse park on the legendary Carretera Austral in the Chacabuco Valley boasts rushing rivers, wide-open steppes and wildlife, including the endangered huemul deer. Named the 2025 World’s Leading Lodge by the World Travel Awards, Explora’s 13-room haven is the only accommodation within its boundaries. Open from September to April, all-inclusive stays here reveal modern, sustainable Chilean design, a spa and outdoor hot tubs, and a front yard known for its prime wildlife viewing.

description: The crown jewel of Austria’s Riviera, Falkensteiner Schlosshotel Velden is an iconic yellow castle gracing Lake Wörthersee’s shores. Dating from the 1590s and rebuilt in 1890, this 105-room retreat seamlessly blends Renaissance grandeur with contemporary elegance. The private beach club offers direct access to Europe’s warmest alpine lake, while the sensory spa delivers signature treatments lakeside. Savor slow-food variations from the Alpe-Adria region at Seespitz Restaurant. This popular filming location and former noble gathering place is mere hours from Vienna, Munich, and Salzburg.

description: Sunlight playing off the grounds at Ferme Saint Siméon might remind you of an impressionist painting. Today, this 17th-century Norman house offers 35 airy accommodations with oak parquet flooring, lush fabrics, and fine furnishings; many overlook the Seine estuary (some of them will propose steam shower and balneo bathtub after refurbishment). The Bistro La Boucane, in the "chaumière of Monet,” and the gastronomic restaurant welcomes you. Enjoy local, seasonal produce by executive chef Matthieu Pouleur.

description: Set atop a craggy hill near the iconic Furore fjord, Furore Grand Hotel makes a swish perch for exploring the Amalfi Coast. Its 35 white-on-white rooms and suites — which cascade down a series of terraces toward the Tyrrhenian Sea — are simply luxurious; some feature private Jacuzzis and plunge pools. The 10,000-square-foot infinity pool is a showstopper, while the subterranean spa cocoons with sumptuous Valmont rituals. Dine al fresco or in the signature restaurant headed by Executive Chef Vincenzo Russo, with culinary consultancy from Michelin‑starred chef Enrico Bartolini.

summary: Antigua An important strategic port and valuable commercial colony since the 1600s, Antigua was known as the “Gateway to the Caribbean” due to its geographic position that offered control over the major sailing routes to and from the region’s rich island colonies. This breathtaking island measures 108 sq. miles and is circled by 95 miles of indented coastline and beaches. The largest of the English-speaking Leeward Islands, Antigua is renowned for its 365 white-sand beaches and impressive maritime history. description: Tucked away in Edinburgh’s bustling St. Andrew’s Square, you’ll find the grand yet intimate Gleneagles Townhouse – a 33-guestroom property with a discreet entrance and glamorous neo-Victorian vibe. Rooms embrace the building’s noble heritage with high ceilings, antique rugs, and free-standing tubs. The all-day restaurant serves international dishes like west coast langoustines and pumpkin and feta tarts. And in the rooftop bar, Lamplighters, you can sip cocktails inspired by author Robert Louis Stevenson, paired with panoramic views of the city.

summary: Gleneagles’ first luxury city hotel, all-day restaurant, roof terrace and members’ club has arrived in St. Andrew Square, Edinburgh. Our 33 guestrooms embrace our noble building’s heritage. Timeless charm blends with all today’s needs in our boutique hotel bedrooms. Deeply comfortable, they’re sanctuaries of downtime as the city sleeps. Great dining and sipping are best savoured in good company. Our all-day restaurant and bar, open to all, is a place for great get-togethers and happy huddles. Our rooftop bar serves classic cocktails and vast views. And private dining is tucked away; as it should be. Gleneagles Townhouse is a place to gather and be glorious.

description: Time seems to stand still at Halekulani Okinawa. summary: Halekulani brings understated, timeless elegance to a setting of breathtaking natural beauty in Okinawa. Guests are invited to explore and discover the soul of these islands in luxurious comfort and seclusion, while experiencing the legendary service for which the Halekulani name is known. Halekulani, from the Hawaiian for ‘House of Befitting Heaven’, has a century-long history on Waikiki Beach, Hawaii in the United States. description: For more than a century, Hotel Barrière Le Normandy has attracted cinematic legends, from Kirk Douglas to Claude Lelouch. And it’s easy to see why. Dive into the private pool, daydream on the Planches boardwalk, place a bet at the Casino and visit the American Film Festival. Deauville is at your door.

description: Barefoot luxury meets Arabian hospitality at InterContinental The Red Sea Resort. description: Lying just across from the Popes’ Palace, La Mirande has gone through many incarnations. You’ll be fascinated by the rich tapestries, indienne fabrics, silk-lined curtains, vintage wallpapers, and Carrara marble, as well as modern touches, such as in-mirror televisions. Take a nightly gastronomic journey in the coffered-ceilinged restaurant; cooking classes teach Provençal secrets with copper pots over the kitchen’s wood-burning stove.

summary: Set in an old mansion at the foot of the Palais des Papes in the heart of Avignon, La Mirande is steeped in secular history. The hotel is named after the famous room in the Palais des Papes, where the Pope’s representatives held receptions for the city’s notables and visiting high-ranking officials. Originally a Cardinal’s Palace in the 14th century, the ruins of La Mirande were restored during the 17th century to create the Hôtel de Vervins and its baroque façade by architect Pierre Mignard, later becoming the Hôtel Pamard between the late 18th and 20th centuries. summary: La Residencia is now open and will close on 15th November, 2026. La Residencia, A Belmond Hotel, is Deià’s intimate mountainside enclave. Art, craft, nature and epicurean cuisine define this Mallorcan retreat, perched between the UNESCO World Heritage Tramuntana Mountains and the Mediterranean Sea. Formerly a hive of agricultural productivity, Deià became world renowned for its creative scene in the last four decades. Under the stewardship of Sir Richard Branson, La Residencia emerged as an artistic hub, attracting musicians, writers and creative souls from around the world. description: Ted Turner operates his empire by a simple motto, “Save Everything” – and once you lay eyes on Ladder, a Ted Turner Reserve, you’ll understand why. The conservationist has diligently preserved the diverse ecosystems comprising his 156,000-acre Ladder Ranch, in south-central New Mexico; the four tributaries of the Rio Grande that traverse the land support abundant flora and fauna, such as historic bison. Turner’s four-bedroom family home features personal mementos; an on-site chef prepares meals to your taste. Expeditions are individually crafted, and all activities are included in your stay.
inTheKnow: The stargazing here is otherworldly; let the ranch arrange for a guest astronomer to guide you across the night skies.
summary: Purchased by Ted Turner in 1992, the Ladder is located in southcentral New Mexico and covers an incredible 156,439 acres (245 square miles). Ladder contains four tributaries of the Rio Grande River – the Animas, Seco, Palomas and Cuchillo streams. These streams support abundant flora, including sycamores and cottonwoods, and fauna such as Chiricahua leopard frogs and sensitive Rio Grande cutthroat trout, which will be soon restored to the streams. description: Dominate the slopes at the 55-room Le Coucou in Méribel. Enjoying unrivalled access to the Trois Vallees, this ski-in/ski-out hotel combines the elegance of a traditional chalet with a playful, contemporary aesthetic that feels cozy and comfortable. You’ll find all the usual powdery play and then some — including paragliding, electric fat bikes, and a double zip-line. description: Set on a secluded beach on Sardinia's Costa Verde — a wilder contrast to the ritzy Costa Smeralda — Le Dune Piscinas is a remote hideaway spotlighting all that makes Sardinia special. With no televisions or distractions — only nature as your soundtrack — each of our Florida Keys resort suites offers space to disconnect, or reconnect with what matters most. A Storied Sanctuary Once a coral reef, then a haven for presidents, poets, and dreamers. Walk the same paths as the legends before you. Stay for the silence that remains.

description: Longitude 131° offers an essential experience of Australia's spiritual heartland. Lounge in the cool sanctuary of the Dune House, relax with an icy drink from the convivial open bar, and dine with ever-changing views of the monolith. After a day's exploring, relax in a luxury tent and enjoy unparalleled views of Uluru from the end of the bed. Retreat to Spa Kinara for an indigenous-inspired treatment or drink in the sunset on the glamorous Dune Top. Venture beyond the lodge to discover the World Heritage-listed wilderness of Uluru-Kata Tjuta and connect with the ancient stories of the land’s traditional owners.

Unparalleled views of Uluru’s changing lights play out from the end of the bed, or on balconies from the warmth of a luxury swag unfurled in the cool night air. It was constructed considering conservation and preservation of the environment. Los Cauquenes Resort + Spa + Experiences offers different activities to live a unique experience: active and adventure tourism, dining experiences, spa and wellness treatments, in/out pool and a unique natural environment.

description: Live life extraordinarily at LUX* Belle Mare. A recent redesign brings fresh energy to this sprawling, 186-key resort, set along its namesake beach on Mauritius' east coast. The reimagined spaces lean into minimal tropical design; there’s a variety of suites and villas ranging from family-friendly to wellness-focused, all centered around the island nation’s largest pools. Go horseback riding, try a healing water therapy, or drift away in a gravity-defying hammock. Culinary offerings range from the Chinese gastronomic restaurant Duck Laundry to Michelin-starred Indian cuisine at Amari by Vineet.
inTheKnow: Belle Mare Beach consistently ranks among the Indian Ocean’s finest. Experience it at Beach Rouge, the resort’s Bohemian-chic beach club and restaurant—you’ll feel transported to Ibiza.
summary: ABOUT LUX* RESORTS & HOTELS Founded in 2011, LUX* is a luxury hospitality brand that challenges the status quo, breaks the rules, rewrites them, and stands out. Spirited, creative, caring, and tasteful, the brand finds its purpose in helping people celebrate life. At LUX* we believe that every single moment is worth celebrating. Worth making remarkable. From life’s big moments to the small ones. Every moment is made extraordinary. Each property celebrates the culture, the people, the nature, and the flavors of the destination it is in.

description: Monasterio, a 1592 monastery turned into a luxury hotel in Cusco, makes it possible for guests to learn about Spanish and Inca cultures during their stay. Enjoy an Andean massage based on a ritual developed by Andes natives; an aromatherapy treatment is administered using qantu, the sacred flower of the Inca. Visit the Lobby Bar for a wide selection of cocktails made from original recipes, and then dine on Peruvian and international dishes at El Tupay restaurant. Take time to meditate on your sacred destination in your Spanish Colonial-Style bedroom, where religious art and local décor adorn the walls.
inTheKnow: Dine outside in the gorgeous courtyard by the ancient fountain if the weather allows; ask for a tour of the hotel if time allows. –Eleanor Hardy Louisville, Kentucky
summary: Looking out of the window at Monasterio, a Belmond Hotel in Cusco, hearts may soar as high as the Andean mountains. The stirring views, together with an authentic immersion in Peruvian culture, make a stay here truly uplifting. Just steps from Cusco’s lively central square, the hotel is set in a restored 16th-century monastery built on the foundations of an Inca palace. From the outside, whitewashed stone walls give little hint as to the splendid interiors within. Guests enter to discover graceful archways, cobbled paths and a cloistered courtyard complete with scented flowerbeds, a fountain and a 300-year-old cedar tree. It’s blissfully tranquil here and Cusco’s altitude is easily managed.…

description: "Peak experience" takes on a whole new meaning at this sanctuary occupying the highest point in Cortona. A former Dominican monastery, the hotel's 36 rooms and suites reflect the space's history as a place of contemplation (most are former friar cells and feature restored vaults and frescoes, as well as views of the Val di Chiana below). Centuries earlier, the site was home to a large cistern called the Bagno di Bacco ("Bacchus' Bath") which is still used as the basis of the modern spa today.

description: Dramatically poised over the Amalfi Coast, a former 17th-century monastery has been reborn as the Monastero Santa Rosa Hotel & Spa. Tiered Mediterranean gardens lead you to the vanishing-edge infinity pool, easily the most dramatic dip along the coast. description: Built in 1852, Mont Cervin Palace stands as the second oldest hotel in Zermatt, and a renovation has given this grande dame a gorgeous new aura. The 150 smartly updated accommodations include cozy chalet rooms with beamed ceilings, as well as family suites with fireplaces, kitchenettes, and whirlpools or saunas. Winter brings tobogganing, ice climbing, and 220 miles of piste play; the summer season offers glacier skiing, hiking, biking, and golf. description: Sir Richard Branson’s love for the African continent and for the finer things in life lured him to the Western Cape province and Mont Rochelle. description: Getting back to nature gets a bespoke update at Morgan’s Rock. Encompassing 4,000 acres – half of which are designated as a protected reserve – this solar-powered jungle hideaway is highlighted by a mile-long stretch of beach, a sustainable farm (with shrimp), and a secluded cove that gives sanctuary to hatching sea turtles. Enjoy the bungalows and villas made of reclaimed wood and bamboo, and featuring plunge pools. Ride horses, go sportfishing, or take a safari to spot howler monkeys and macaws. Practice your swing on the driving range, the first within a UNESCO World Heritage site. Afterward, soak in your Jacuzzi or relax with a massage, either in your room or on a scenic terrace.

description: Set just off popular Platis Gialos Beach away from Mykonos’ party scene, the uber-chic Myconian Ambassador offers an idyllic blend of cool sophistication and warm Cycladic charm. Feel the flow in 69 open-concept accommodations featuring private balconies and heart-palpitating views; most have an outdoor Jacuzzi or plunge pool. The signature restaurant, Efisia, boasts Relais & Châteaux bona fides for regional fare that relies on seasonal, organic produce and the catch of the day. You may never want to leave the expansive pool deck, although the hotel has a private launch for a visit to ancient Delos.

summary: The Ambassador is a luxury hotel in Mykonos, capturing the essence of Myconian charm and the celebrated ‘art de vivre’ of Relais & Châteaux. Interiors that embody the clean line and cool sophistication of high design flow into the quiet comfort of luxurious bedrooms, or spill out onto the spectacular terrace that is the heart of the hotel, all without ever breaking the spell of magnificent Aegean views. description: Apollo, the Greek god of healing, was said to be born on the island of Delos, which fronts Mykonos Grand Hotel & Resort. The 96 rooms and suites are generously sized, with clean, streamlined decor; some even have private pools. Get a therapeutic spa treatment by the pool or in a seaside cabana, take a leisurely stroll into charming Hora – Mykonos Town – or swim in the 500-square-meter, heated outdoor pool. The open-air signature restaurant delivers fine Greek fare with dramatic sunsets.

description: Nayara grounds are bursting with wildlife. You can spot sloths and monkeys on our trails, or join a bird-watching walk at dawn. After dark, you can join a frog scouting tour where you can see diminutive red-eyed tree frogs and blue-jean frogs in our ponds. Our resort is also a botanist and gardener’s paradise. Our trails are teeming with tropical plants and exotic flowers, from heliconias and orchids to cacao and plantain trees. Our Armadillo Trail showcases fruit trees on both sides of the winding path.

Read in the comfort of your hammock, or unwind on the balcony listening to the birds and crickets. After dark, take a walk with a naturalist guide to experience the unique on-property frog watching night tour. summary: Nayara Tented Camp was built on stilts to maximize the stunning vistas and leave a minimal footprint. The experience is secluded and romantic for couples, or fun and educational for the whole family. Inspired in the African safaris but conceived in the tropical Costa Rican rainforest, the tents are a mix of sustainable luxury with a “Pura Vida” vibe. If a soothing soak is a staple in your self-care routine, prepare to swoon over the tub; or if an outdoor shower with the stars is your thing, you will have a lifetime experience. A great place to reset and recharge, far from civilization and close to nature, and with great sleep helped by the calming sounds of the rainforest.

description: Every tatami mat, shoji screen, and lavish kaiseki dinner reveals a peek inside Nishimuraya Honkan’s 160-year history. The ryokan (Japanese-style inn) traditional architecture transports you into another era – one with lush gardens, indoor and outdoor hot springs, and artfully-crafted multi-course meals featuring Matsuba crab (winter only), Tajima beef, and Konotori rice served in the privacy of your room. Don’t miss the two-level museum showcasing an expansive collection of local photos, paintings, and relics.

summary: Nishimuraya Honkan is part of Virtuoso’s exclusive Regional Program for Asia. description: San Sebastian is one of Europe’s major gastronomic capitals, making it the perfect location for the newest Nobu Hotel. Here, guests can savor signature dishes like black cod miso and tuna sashimi tacos, while indulging in views of La Concha Bay. The 17 modern-meets-minimalist rooms and suites offer a welcomed culinary intermission offering amenities like high-thread count linens, rainfall showers, and access to the hotel’s rooftop pool and 24-hour fitness center.
inTheKnow: Continue your foodie fix at San Sebastian’s buzzing pintxos bars or one of the city’s eight Michelin-starred restaurants.
summary: Where culture and gastronomy meet sleek design, Nobu Hotel San Sebastián, is a luxurious lifestyle destination, located in the heart of the one of the gastronomic capitals of Europe. Overlooking the stunning La Concha Bay, the hotel offers 17 stylish, spacious guest rooms and suites with exquisite beach views, amid an area famed for its cultural diversity and culinary excellence. The iconic Nobu restaurant offers views over the city’s main beach, La Concha, that are unsurpassed. Situated within walking distance of all the city’s attractions, Nobu San Sebastián offers an opportunity to enjoy the beautiful destination while experiencing Nobu’s exceptional service, food, and style.

description: Nobu Ryokan Malibu pays homage to the traditional Japanese inn while giving it a haute makeover. Super chef Nobu Matsuhisa and superstar Robert De Niro reimagined a historic 1950s motel on exclusive Carbon Beach (aka “Billionaire’s Beach”) into a California lifestyle-conscious retreat. Tatami mats, fireplaces, and original prints inspire serenity in the 16 rooms, as do the teak tubs set beneath skylights, creating the sense of soaking outdoors. Do your sun salutation on the spacious beachfront deck, and dine in your suite with a custom menu from Nobu Malibu restaurant next door.
inTheKnow: Garden Rooms create an even deeper connection to nature with unique floor plans that create a flow between indoor space and the outdoor Zen garden with meditation pool.
summary: Drifting above the Pacific, the Nobu Ryokan Malibu is a triumph of architectural carpentry and subdued hospitality. This intimate 16 room retreat honors the traditional Japanese Ryokan, featuring teak soaking tubs, indoor/outdoor fireplaces, serene outdoor patios, timeless artwork and gracious accents. From the moment you arrive, the unforgettable views of Pacific Ocean and tranquil landscaping sets the tone for a private oasis. Exclusivity and privacy are foremost, with an emphasis on low-key comfort and high-end indulgence. A host of luxurious amenities awaits you, coupled with gracious service and Nobu comforts.

description: Orient Express Venezia occupies a 15th-century noble residence that once lodged the Duke of Urbino. Set along the Grand Canal in the quiet Cannaregio district, this magnificently restored palace awes guests with its marbled facade, neo-Gothic octagonal staircase, vaulted ceilings, exquisite statues, and colorful frescos. The 45 elegantly detailed rooms and suites overlook gardens and the canals. Sip a Venetian spritz in the bar before dining on fine Italian fare in the outstanding restaurant.
inTheKnow: Head to one of the hotel’s hidden rooftop terraces for stunning views that stretch across Venice’s UNESCO-designated lagoon.
summary: A 15th-century Venetian palace reawakens after an eight-year renovation by architect Aline Asmar d’Amman. The Palace was transformed in the 1800s by architect Gian Battista Meduna and beautified with layers of Neo-Gothic and Baroque splendor. Once home to the Duke of Urbino and the Donà and Giovannelli families, it later became a Pinacoteca. Now, through Orient Express, it begins a new hospitality chapter, honoring the legacy of a noble mansion while embracing the spirit of the iconic hotel brand. Just ten minutes from the historic quay, the palace gleams anew, its courtyard, terraces, and garden inviting exploration.

description: Echoes of ancient chariots rise from the Colosseum, which appears to be within arm’s reach of Palazzo Manfredi. (A gladiator school once stood a few meters from where the hotel now stands.) Yet this 16th-century palazzo dazzles with more than just its jaw-dropping views. The 15 rooms and five suites fuse Palladian wallpaper, faux fur, Roman busts, and eel-skin-topped tables to surprisingly successful effect; windows overlooking the monument are a must. summary: Palazzo Manfredi is an elegant hideaway in the center of what was once imperial Rome. The charming 17th century palace has spectacular views of the Colosseum, the Forum, and the Domus Aurea, combined with superb hospitality. Built over the ruins of the Ludus Magnus, the gymnasium used by Roman gladiators, Palazzo Manfredi was the hunting pavilion of the Guidi gardens. Today it is tastefully adorned with art ranging from 16th century antique paintings to contemporary pieces. The hotel offers an intimate experience, crowned only by a meal at the hotel’s Aroma restaurant where the unparalleled vistas of ancient Rome are beautifully matched by the culinary delights. description: Palazzo Margherita is the realization of renowned director Francis Ford Coppola’s dream to convert a 19th-century palazzo in his grandfather’s charming hometown into a luxurious boutique hotel; the restoration took five years. summary: Palazzo Margherita, built in 1892 in Bernalda by the Margherita family, is a true 19th century palazzo. The town was the birthplace and home to Agostino Coppola, Francis Ford Coppola';s grandfather, who always referred to it affectionately as "Bernalda bella." Francis purchased the Palazzo in 2004 with the desire to transform it into a small, luxurious hotel, believing it was time to introduce visitors to this stunning and still undiscovered region. Nestled between the ancient cities of Metapontum and Matera, the area is rich with history, including haunting primordial cave dwellings called Sassi di Matera, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. description: If past is prologue, then Baltimore’s future looks bright indeed thanks to Pendry Baltimore. The historic Recreation Pier (where immigrants once arrived) has been transformed into a 128-room boutique hotel that stays true to its roots while delivering plenty of modern conveniences. Icons of glory days are sprinkled about, from images of blue crabs and Edgar Allan Poe to a 17th-century cannon under glass in the moody Cannon Bar. The rustic-glam Rec Pier Chop House quickly has become the city’s top spot for Italian, and locals often linger over crafted sips by the infinity pool, which appears to float on the harbor.
inTheKnow: Ask The Cannon Room’s sommelier to lead you through a tasting of the bar’s curated menu of premium whiskeys, including the locally brewed Sagamore rye.
summary: Defining what’s old is new again. Poised in the storied 1914 property on Baltimore’s historic Recreation Pier – “Rec Pier” as it’s known to locals – Pendry Baltimore embodies the city’s rich history, vibrant personality and idyllic harbor setting with character, inspiration and style. Rooted in tradition and re-imagined for today, the pier’s extensive renovation honored the historic essence of the property and restored its former glory, reflecting a bygone era, impeccable service, unparalleled quality and travel that inspires through modern sensibility and aesthetics that speaks to today’s guest.

description: Raise a flute to Royal Champagne Hotel & Spa. The UNESCO-designated wine region’s first destination spa pays fizzy tribute to the historic vineyards that lie just beyond its infinity-edge pool and walls of windows. Forty-seven rooms and suites are spread across the original 19th-century coaching inn and a modernist wing crafted from glass and local quartz. Look for bubbles everywhere – in the metalwork, light fixtures in the one-Michelin-starred restaurant, and wall etchings in the rooms. Shimmery golden wallpaper adds an effervescent touch to myBlend and Clarins Precious spa treatments.

Come for the bubbles, stay for the journey!

description: More than just the food comes farm-fresh at São Lourenço do Barrocal. There is a natural elegance to the entire lifestyle at this rustic retreat, a family-run, working estate located in southeastern Portugal. Here, guests are invited to hit pause and reset amid the rural Alentejo landscape, wandering among the ancient holm oaks, olive groves, and private vineyard, or perhaps picnicking in a wildflower-filled meadow. The 40 rooms and cottages reveal artisan touches, with handmade-brick floors and an eclectic mix of homey pieces. Spa therapies utilize exclusive cosmetics from the organic Austrian brand Susanne Kaufmann.

summary: A LITTLE ABOUT US São Lourenço do Barrocal is a hotel and monte alentejano, located in a wild corner of the Alentejo, Portugal, in the foothills of medieval Monsaraz and nearby the Alqueva lake. description: Discover a timeless grandeur in Japan’s ancient capital at Shisui, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Nara. Housed in the former governor’s residence inside leafy Nara Park — noted for its serene temples and resident deer — the hotel blends historical elements with clean, contemporary stylings in its 43 light-filled accommodations; some feature natural hot spring baths. Revitalize with an indigenous spa treatment before enjoying free-flowing champagne and dinner overlooking adjacent Yoshikien Gardens. Nara’s UNESCO World Heritage-designated monuments are within walking distance.
inTheKnow: Immerse yourself in the local culture with an ink-making class, morning yoga session in Yoshikien Gardens, guided tour of Nara Park, or rickshaw ride around the city’s heritage sites.
summary: Shisui, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Nara is part of Virtuoso’s exclusive Regional Program for Asia. Nestled on the western edge of Nara Park, one of Japan’s most famous scenic spots, the Yoshikien area where our Nara luxury hotel is located is surrounded by World Heritage Sites such as Kasuga Taisha Shrine, Kofukuji Temple, and Todaiji Temple, and has been protected by efforts to maintain the area’s lush greenery to ensure a scenic and serene environment. The name of the hotel derives from the “purple trunk and green leaves (Shikan Suiyou)” – scenic vistas that have been cherished in Nara since ancient times. description: Sina Brufani has counted the queen mother of England and the prince of Monaco among its esteemed guests, and considers it a true honor to host many of the world’s most discriminating travelers. Here in the center of historic Perugia, this intimate hideaway offers 94 traditional yet modern guest rooms, the renowned Collins’ Restaurant, and an enchanting view of the Umbrian Valley. Locals flock to the outdoor terrace during the summertime, partaking of the delicious regional cuisine and refined wines. Of particular note is the indoor swimming pool; ancient Etruscan ruins are displayed under its transparent glass floor.
inTheKnow: The staff goes out of its way to make children feel welcome; the maître d’ will have the restaurant prepare whatever foods even your pickiest eaters desire.
summary: The Sina Brufani is located in the heart of Perugia’s ancient city center, one of Umbria’s most prestigious landmarks. Umbria, which is called “The green heart of Italy”, is primarily characterized by its quintessential countryside landscapes and by its artistic and historical heredity. Assisi, Todi, Spoleto, Gubbio and Spello are just a stone’s throw away from Perugia and worth a daytrip visit. summary: Once Palazzo Genovese, today Sina Centurion Palace. A 5 star luxury hotel located on the Grand Canal with stunning views of both the Grand Canal and the traditional venetian internal garden. The Hotel is located in the heart of the Dorsoduro district next to the Basilica of S. Maria della Salute, Punta della Dogana and the famous Guggenheim museum. A unique blend between the ancient building’s gothic façade and the contemporary exclusive bespoke design of the interiors; a contrast in harmony with the district where the hotel is located; the most ancient in Venice and home to contemporary art.

description: For those who see health and happiness as a journey of discovery, not a destination, Six Senses Bhutan offers uplifting experiences at every turn. The circuit immerses guests into Bhutan’s spirituality, culture, and hospitality as they travel between five individual lodges. Experiences include a sunrise meditation in Thimpu, afternoon cocktails riverside in a rice field in Punakha, watching Tibetan black-necked cranes at Gangtey, indulging in hot-stone baths at Bumthang, and gathering to dine and celebrate life in the stone ruins of Paro. You’ll leave feeling enlightened and reconnected (while not really wishing to leave at all).
inTheKnow: You may visit a single lodge or, if you're curious about everything that Bhutan has to offer, we can plan a tailor-made Mindful Journeys that will include a combination of 5 locations.
summary: Six Senses Bhutan will move you – to pause and think. This colorful Himalayan Kingdom lives by its ethos of gross national happiness. Journey through the vertiginous scenery of the western and central valleys, and you can’t help but find meaningful and uplifting experiences at every turn. That’s why our guest suites are distributed between five intimate lodges. Each has a unique character and all embrace our Six Senses guiding principles, which include a Six Senses Spa and Wellness Center, mindful eating, sleep and self-discovery. Part of a UNESCO World Heritage site, this 810-acre estate features the recently opened 27-bedroom Son Bunyola Hotel and three standalone luxury villas. summary: Honoring the history of the landmark L. Mendel Rivers Federal Building (circa 1964), The Dewberry captures the luxury and quiet restraint that are hallmarks of historic Charleston. The result is a thoughtfully imagined juxtaposition of past and present that redefines what is possible when historic preservation is paramount.

description: The Fife Arms is far more than a 19th-century landmark hotel; it is a living museum of Braemar history. Timber and other materials in the newly built section are locally sourced, as are most of the fresh seafood and game, seasonal produce, and over 300 varieties of whisky. Explore the extensive network of hill trails; get an acupressure massage; or visit nearby Balmoral Castle, open to the public April through July.

summary: Built in the 19th century, The Fife Arms Hotel is a Braemar landmark and is a category B listed building. The building has retained all of its timber sash and case windows with their distinctive Arts and Crafts multi-paned upper sashes, and a large number of original chimney stacks. The hotel boasts a unique location overlooking Victoria Falls. The 173 luxurious rooms are elegantly furnished, featuring a balcony or veranda with outdoor seating, overlooking lush gardens frequented by free-roaming zebras, giraffes, and impalas. All guests have unlimited access to Victoria Falls, a short walk through the grounds, and entry through a private gate into the Falls.

The Hotel consists of a series of 17 buildings, with deep verandas, set amidst indigenous trees and plants. The main hotel is a sequence of thatch-roofed buildings, most African in their influence, and incorporates the lounge, The Old Drift restaurant and Travellers Bar. Here you can enjoy simple luxury as you gaze upon the fjords outside your picture window. Take advantage of a wide variety of excursions – more than 20. Go sailing or trek to prehistoric caves. Kayak, fly-fish, spot condors, and travel on horseback to the top of Cerro Tenerife.

description: The adobe walls of an ancient cattle corral blend into Tierra Atacama, a tribute to the indigenous people who once inhabited this surreal landscape. That sense of place is evident everywhere in this glass-walled, 28-room marvel, from the artisan-crafted furnishings to the native medicinal plants in the gardens. Explore the area’s salt pans, volcanoes, and geyser fields on hikes, horseback rides, and more, then return to get an activity-focused spa treatment, relax in a basket swing, or lounge by the pool. The vibe is totally casual; the locally sourced cuisine and wines, simply divine.

description: Set atop Fourvière Hill near the ancient Roman theatres, Villa Maïa provides a chic perch above Lyon’s UNESCO-inscribed old town. The 33 sophisticated rooms and suites blend Japanese-inspired aesthetics with a hint of Art Deco and high attention to detail; private terraces overlook the serene gardens and red-roofed Vieux-Lyon. Ancient vaults now house Les Thermes, a modern take on the Roman bath with a hammam, jacuzzi, and majestic indoor pool. summary: In the heart of Lyon The History... Time stands still on the hill of Fourvière. The birthplace of Gallo-Roman civilisation, Fourvière stands guard over the city of Lyon in a conventual silence. Known to locals as the “hill that prays”, it is a uniquely serene and spiritual place. Maïa Group chairman Christophe Gruy fell in love with it. And Villa Maïa is the result. A sumptuously intimate hotel, dreamt up, designed and decorated by Jean-Michel Wilmotte, Jacques Grange and Louis Benech. An unprecedented trio brought together for Villa Maïa.

description: Zannier Île de Bendor reimagines the storied Île de Bendor off Provence’s Bandol coast. Exuding the playful spirit of the South of France, this boutique resort sprawls village-style across the private, car-free island; its 93 keys are housed in three characteristic buildings ranging from vintage 1960s glamour to traditional Provençal fishermen’s houses along the harbor. Amenities include a beach club, curated artisan village, holistic wellness center, and an array of dining and beverage options, along with a diving center and other leisure facilities.
inTheKnow: Be prepared for day-trippers visiting the island — but rest assured, overnight guests enjoy exclusive after-hours tranquility.
summary: Zannier Île de Bendor, newly opened in May 2026 Our new stylish 93-key hotel, Zannier Île de Bendor opened its doors on May 1st, 2026 after a five-year transformation of Île de Bendor, one of the Côte d’Azur’s most famous private islands. With design and ambience rooted in the spirit of conviviality, the truly one-of-a-kind immersive destination will bring a new social, culinary and wellness capital to the Mediterranean.

description: Find renewal at Zulal Wellness Resort by Chiva-Som, the Middle East’s largest wellness destination. Rooted in Traditional Arabic and Islamic Medicine (TAIM), the resort blends ancient healing wisdom with modern holistic therapies on Qatar’s tranquil northern coast. The resort features 94 Serenity rooms and suites for adults and 86 Discovery rooms and suites for families. Guests can enjoy 200+ wellness treatments and distinctive facilities including the Arctic Cave, Plunge Pool, Himalayan Salt Room, holistic Apothecary, Tea House, specialised Aesthetics, Longevity and Cosmetic services, alongside dedicated Family Wellness experiences.
